summary.headline: Nitin Spinners Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR875 crore (+10.3% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 17.78%, with PAT up 83.6% to INR75.3 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue of INR875 crore was the company's highest ever quarter for a second straight quarter, up 10.3% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, driven mainly by yarn realisations. EBITDA before other income was INR155.6 crore (+39.85% YoY), with margin at 17.78% versus 14.02% a year earlier and 15.17% in the prior quarter. Management attributed the margin gain mostly to yarn price realisation outpacing cotton cost, with smaller contributions from power cost savings and efficiency. Management guided that the new capacities (fabric +35 million metres, spinning +74,000 spindles) will add INR200-300 crore revenue in the near term, though the commissioning timeline has since been reset.

segments.name: Spinning (yarn)
segments.commentary: Running at 98% utilisation. Yarn spread (yarn price less cotton) reported at about INR130/kg currently versus about INR110 in the prior quarter. Management said yarn price increases outpaced cotton, and a fall in outside yarn sales was due to higher in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit.

segments.name: Woven fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation above 92%. Fabric margins have not expanded like yarn; pass-through is only of actual cotton increases. Fabric revenue was about INR700 crore plus in FY26 and is about 20-21% of revenue, targeted at about 30% after expansion.

segments.name: Knitted fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation at about 55-60%, below the pre-US-tariff norm of 60-65%, because of US tariff uncertainty; the US had been a major market for knit fabric.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stay in the company's 16-20% band; management said it aims for the upper end but gave no firm guidance on reaching it. Management said it expects current margins to be maintained, and declined to comment on improvement.

Renewable power capacity expected operational by end Q3 FY27; management estimates about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit, with about INR1.2-1.5 crore already in Q1 and an analyst assumption of about INR12.5 crore per quarter from Q4.
Blended power cost expected around INR5.50/unit once solar covers about 60% of requirements.

New capacity: weaving starts in about two months, processing in about 1.5 months later (around Diwali), spinning on stream by about December; utilisation to ramp to 31 March 2027, with fabric 100% ramp taking a quarter or two into FY28.

Expansion adds about INR1,000-1,100 crore of turnover at full run-rate, of which about INR500 crore is fabric (FY28 fabric revenue targeted at INR1,200 crore) and yarn about 40% for external sale; management said incremental fabric revenue is 'not factoring in' the price volatility.
Management said no new capex is planned until after FY28 beyond the announced expansion.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion of 35 million metres (weaving plus finishing; solid and yarn-dyed fabrics; no printing capacity added).
Spinning expansion of 74,000 spindles; about 22,000 metric tons of new yarn capacity, of which 16,000-18,000 MT goes into fabric and some to yarn dyeing.
Capex of about INR1,100 crore; Rajasthan textile scheme incentives apply, with capital subsidy booked in other income.
Renewable power expansion on schedule for end Q3 FY27.
Spinning utilisation 98%; woven fabric utilisation over 92%; knit fabric 55-60%.
demand_pricing: Cotton prices rose about 8-10% in Q1 on lower global output and West Asia-related logistics issues; India removed cotton import duty.
Indian cotton had been priced above the Cotlook index in 2023-24 (about +5-7%); it now trades at about -1 to -2% versus Cotlook, a delta of about 7-8 points.
Indian yarn exports to China rose to about 110-115 million kg in CY26 from 90-100 million kg in 2025; management sees China's import demand continuing.
Management said spinning capacity exits in the last 1-2 years and the post-US-tariff demand slump have rebalanced supply.

Volumes: management said yarn outside sales fell because of in-house consumption by fabric units and about some stock held at quarter-end due to vessel shortages; these were said to have dispatched in July.
Price pass-through: yarn price increases exceeded cotton increases (management cited about 120-125% pass-through on a 100% cotton increase); fabric pass-through is only 1:1 on cotton.
India crop: about 318-320 lakh bales for 2025-26, versus 326-327 lakh bales in 2024-25; 2026-27 acreage about 0.5-1% lower; rainfall over the next month is the key factor.

qa_highlights.question: What are the yarn spreads in Q1 and Q2 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about INR110 in the last quarter of FY26 and are now about INR130, and management said this is sustained at current conditions.

qa_highlights.question: Are current margins of 17-18% sustainable for the next one to two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to maintain the current level, with cost savings helping, but declined to comment on any further improvement or on a decline.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 EBITDA expansion is from power savings, realisation, and inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Power savings contributed about 0.5% of EBITDA and a similar amount from solar; the gross margin rise to about 40% came mainly from yarn realisation. Inventory gains were described as very small, and the working capital cycle is broadly unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What share of new capacity revenue goes to fabric, and how fast will it ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: About 600-plus crore of the expansion's turnover is fabric, with yarn ramp-up complete by 31 March 2027 and fabric taking a quarter or two more into FY28; fabric revenue is expected at INR1,200 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company consider a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, as it is in a growth phase funding capex through internal accruals and loans, so a buyback would not be prudent now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning garmenting or home textiles as the next growth leg?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said garmenting is only an idea with nothing firmed up, and home textiles and garmenting are both seen as equally good opportunities, with Europe the key opening for home textiles after the US slump.

risks_watch: Commissioning timeline: weaving in about two months, processing about 1.5 months later, spinning by about December; fabric ramp-up may take a quarter or two into FY28 (management also cited 6-8 months for fabric ramp-up in one answer).

Cotton price volatility and pass-through: fabric margins expand only 1:1 with cotton, while yarn spread (about INR130/kg) is sustained only under current conditions; management declined to commit to margin levels beyond maintaining current ones.
US tariff uncertainty keeps knitted fabric utilisation at about 55-60% versus 60-65% pre-tariff norm; knit fabric exposure to the US remains a drag.
Monsoon/rainfall over the next month will determine the 2026-27 Indian cotton crop size; quality outlook depends on the same.
Yarn outside-sales volumes fell QoQ and YoY due to in-house fabric consumption and stock in transit; shipment logistics (vessel availability) to be monitored for July dispatches.

Renewable power capacity due by end Q3 FY27; about INR50 crore annual EBITDA benefit is management's estimate, and the blended power cost target of about INR5.50/unit depends on solar covering about 60% of requirements.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and the capacity build-out, with specific figures on spreads, utilisation and power costs. Cautious and evasive on forward margins: it would only say it expects to maintain current levels, declined to comment on improvement or on any decline, and gave no firm timeline for reaching the upper end of the 16-20% band.
